evals.prompt:
I have this Python code that fetches 50 URLs sequentially and it's way too slow:

```python
results = []
for url in urls:
    results.append(fetch_url(url))  # async def fetch_url(url) -> str
```

Make it concurrent, but if one fetch fails I don't want it to kill everything else — collect whatever succeeded. Also make sure we never have more than 10 requests in flight at once because the API rate-limits us.
evals.expected_output: Code using Semaphore(10) around each fetch plus either TaskGroup or gather(return_exceptions=True), with correct handling so failures don't cancel siblings; explanation of why gather alone without return_exceptions would leave other tasks running.

evals.prompt:
Review this asyncio snippet for bugs:

```python
import asyncio, time

async def worker(q):
    while True:
        item = await q.get()
        time.sleep(item)
        print('done', item)

async def main():
    q = asyncio.Queue()
    for i in range(5):
        q.put_nowait(i)
    t = asyncio.create_task(worker(q))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    # assume program ends here

asyncio.run(main())
```
evals.expected_output: Identifies: (1) time.sleep blocks the event loop — should be asyncio.sleep or to_thread; (2) missing queue.task_done(); (3) fire-and-forget task not awaited/strongly referenced; (4) no graceful shutdown of the infinite worker loop.

evals.prompt: Write a Python asyncio producer/consumer system: one producer generates jobs into a bounded queue (max 100 items for backpressure), 4 consumers process them, and when production finishes the whole thing shuts down cleanly — consumers exit after draining remaining items. Target Python 3.12. Show me the full runnable script.
evals.expected_output: Bounded Queue(maxsize=100); 4 consumer tasks; clean shutdown either via sentinel-per-worker or (better) noting shutdown() is 3.13+ and using sentinels/cancellation for 3.12; task_done/join bookkeeping or equivalent; workers reaped properly.
